My name is **Pierre**, nice to meet you all! I'm currently working as a research engineer in Inria/INSA team **Emeraude**, working among other things on a PhD Thesis intitled *Compilation and Optimization methods for Digital Audio Signal Processing and Synthesis on hardware architectures*. I'm mainly a **software engineer**, a bit specialized in **audio** and **compilation**, I'm involved in the development/maintenance of tools such as: - **Syfala** (Faust-to-FPGA compilation toolchain) - **FloPoCo/HAriCo** (Hardware Arithmetic Core Generator) - **Emeraude-MLIR** (Compilation framework) - **Faust** (but not really...) ## Learning audio DSP & synthesis stuff ## Agenda ::: {style="font-size: 20%;"}
::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### **October** ::: {style="font-size: 80%;"} - Tuesday **20th** 14h-18h (4 hours) ::: ::: {style="font-size: 20%;"}
::: ### **November** ::: {style="font-size: 80%;"} - Tuesday **3rd**: 9h-12h (3 hours) - Thursday **5th**: 13h-16h - Tuesday **10th**: 9h-12h - Thursday **12th**: 13h-16h - Tuesday **17th**: 9h-12h - Thursday **19th**: 13h-16h - Tuesday **24th**: 9h-12h - Thursday **26th**: 13h-16h ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### **December** ::: {style="font-size: 80%;"} - Tuesday **1st**: 9h-12h - Thursday **3rd**: 13h-16h ::: ::: {style="font-size: 20%;"}
::: ### **Evaluation** - ? ::: :::: ## Sound (physical properties) :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.content style="padding-left: -50px;"} ::: {style="font-size: 90%;"} - Sound is a **pressure wave**, that propagates through a **medium** (gas, liquid, or solid). - Propagation is caused by the **oscillation** (*vibration*) of the medium's particles, around their equilibrium positions. - Sound has the following properties: - **Speed**: ~343m/s in air - **Amplitude**: measured in Pascals (Pa) - **Period**: time between two oscillations - **Wavelength**: distance between two oscillations - **Frequency**: cycles per second, in Hertz (Hz, kHz, MHz) - **Spectrum** (or timbre) ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ANIMATIONS ::: :::: ## Sound perception
- Our perception of sound is made from the conversion of the **vibrations** reaching our **eardrums** to a **signal of nerve impulses**, transmitted and interpreted by the brain. - Human ears can typically identify sounds ranging from **20 Hz to 20 kHz**. - Other animal ranges: - **Bat**: 2 kHz to 110 kHz, - **Porpoise**: 75 Hz to 150 kHz, - **Cat**: 45 Hz to 64 kHz, - **Dog**: 67 Hz to 45 kHz, - **Chicken**: 125 Hz to 2 kHz ## Signal - A signal describes the **evolution** of a certain type of *data* **over time**, like the vibration of an entity: the **membrane of a microphone**. - Just like sound waves turning into nerve impulses, the analyzed data usually needs to be first **converted to another physical unit**, or domain (transduction), in order to adapt to measurement/processing tools. - The vibration of a microphone's membrane is, for instance, usually converted to **continuous electrical current** before it can be processed and/or analyzed. In this case, the signal is said to be ***analog***. ## Signal - With an **oscilloscope**, we can measure the **amplitude of a signal** at a given point in time (***time-domain***), through the visualisation of its ***waveform***. - An analog signal can already be processed as it is with **analog effects**: *tape delay*, *distortion*, *chorus*, *reverberation *(spring, plate), etc. - On the other hand, it is difficult to extract precise information about **frequency and spectrum**. For this purpose, it's far more efficient to switch to the ***frequency domain***, which requires the analog signal to be **turned into a digital signal**... ## Digital Signal - To *digitize* a continuous signal implies ***discretizing it***. This is made possible by an **Analog-to-Digital Conversion** (**ADC**) process, which implies two key elements: ***sampling*** and ***quantization***. - **Sampling** means taking a sample of a signal at a certain frequency/rate (***sample rate***). - **Audio CD**: 44.1 kHz - **Pro Audio**: 48/96 kHz - **MP3 (compressed)**: 320/256/192/128/96/64 kbps - Because of ***aliasing*** the sampling rate must be ***at least two times superior to the highest frequency*** we want to represent (**Nyquist-Shannon**) ## Faust - **FAUST** (Functional Audio Stream) is a programming language specifically made for audio DSP and synthesis. It was created by **Yann Orlarey**, **Dominique Fober** & **Stéphane Letz** at **GRAME** in 2002. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} - Functional paradigm, - Declarative, math-like syntax - Produces optimized code for many architectures - Not recommended (yet) for multi-rate (FFT) ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - Plugins: VST, CLAP, AudioUnit - Software: JUCE, Max, Pd, SuperCollider, Csound - OS: Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, - Embedded: Bela, Teensy, Daisy, ESP32, FPGA... - Code: C/C++, Rust, WASM, Java... ::: - Tutorials & documentation available at https://faust.grame.fr - Dedicated online IDE: https:://faustide.grame.fr :::: ## Test {{< include faust/basics.qmd >}}
